context7.description: Live documentation lookup for libraries/frameworks - no API key required

firecrawl.description: Self-hosted Firecrawl (see scripts/setup-firecrawl.sh and its section in .env.example), verified working via a live scrape smoke test. USE_DB_AUTHENTICATION=false in this setup so no FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is needed; add one back if you turn auth on. To use Firecrawl Cloud instead, drop FIRECRAWL_API_URL and set a real FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.

obsidian.description: Read/search/write your Obsidian vault via librarian-mcp (github.com/ngmeyer/librarian-mcp) - reads the vault folder straight off disk, so Obsidian does not need to be running (and it doesn't matter what OS Obsidian itself runs on). Ships native binaries for Linux/macOS/Windows. Under WSL2, point this at the /mnt/c/... path if your vault lives on the Windows side rather than a Windows-style path - see AGENTS.md. Chosen over MarkusPfundstein/mcp-obsidian (see AGENTS.md) for that reason plus a richer tool set: trigram search, auto-wikilinks on write, and real graph analytics (Louvain communities, PageRank, shortest-path). Install: curl -fsSL https://github.com/ngmeyer/librarian-mcp/releases/latest/download/librarian-mcp-installer.sh | sh

browser-use.description: Low-level browser control (browser_exec/browser_screenshot) backed by browser-use's Chromium-based "browser harness" - Claude Code itself decides the steps by writing the automation code, rather than browser-use running its own internal LLM agent. No API key of any kind needed, unlike browser-use's other MCP mode (--mcp, an autonomous agent hardcoded to OpenAI - see AGENTS.md). --python 3.12 is pinned because browser-use needs >=3.11 and uvx isn't guaranteed to pick a satisfying interpreter on its own (see AGENTS.md). Requires `uv`/`uvx` on PATH (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Chromium installed once via `uvx browser-use[cli] install` (may prompt for sudo on Linux - see AGENTS.md, not something setup.sh/setup.ps1 run for you). Complements lightpanda below (this drives a real Chromium via exec'd Python; that one is a lighter, text-oriented engine for deterministic scraping).

lightpanda.description: Lightpanda's own native MCP server (stdio) - fast/cheap deterministic scraping without a full Chrome. Superseded the @playwright/mcp + --cdp-endpoint approach: that path is broken (Lightpanda emits no Page lifecycle events, so every Playwright navigation times out - see AGENTS.md), while this native surface (tree/markdown/html/findElement/evaluate/extract/...) drives Lightpanda's engine directly and works, verified by scripts/test-mcp.py. No separate `lightpanda serve` process or port needed - the stdio subprocess owns its own browser instance for the session. Install: curl -fsSL https://pkg.lightpanda.io/install.sh | bash

codegraph.description: Codebase knowledge graph - search/context/callers/callees/impact/explore/node/files/status. Already installed locally (v1.5.0); run `codegraph init` in a project once to build its index. Generated via `codegraph install --print-config claude`.

_comments.usage: Copy the servers you need into ~/.claude.json's mcpServers section, or register the same command/args/env/url through the Bifrost UI (Settings -> MCP -> Add Server; see https://docs.getbifrost.ai).
